question.text: Asha Deep Trust, a women-empowerment NPO incorporated in June 2023, approaches Mr. Arjun Desai (SIA) in August 2025 for pre-registration review on BSE SSE. Mr. Desai examines the registration-age criterion under the mandatory qualification table. Which statement is CORRECT?

answer.text: Asha Deep Trust is NOT eligible — the registration certificate of the NPO must be at least 3 years old.
Asha Deep Trust is eligible because 2 years of operations is sufficient for SSE registration.
Asha Deep Trust is eligible only if it submits 5 years of audited accounts.
Age of the NPO is not a criterion; only Section 12A registration age matters.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Table 3.1 of the SSE Guidebook (Reg 292F(1)) mandates a MINIMUM 3 years age of the NPO, evidenced by the registration certificate. An NPO incorporated in June 2023 is only ~2 years and 2 months old in August 2025 and therefore fails the age test. The SIA should decline the pre-listing attestation until the entity crosses 3 years. **The Trap:** Option A confuses 2 yrs with 3 yrs. Option C imports an 'audited accounts' count (3 yrs of audited financials is separate). Option D is wrong — both the NPO age AND the 12A validity (next 12 months) are independent requirements. **Cross-Exam Context:** V-A (MF Distributor) does not test NPO age. X-A (IA L1) advisors may recommend older NPOs for CSR eligibility under Section 135 (which has its own 3-year track requirement) — XXIII tests the SSE-specific limb. III-A touches listing-period track records. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Always date-arithmetic the registration certificate against the SSE application date, not the review date. Some NPOs reconstitute from society to Section-8 company — clarify whether the 3-year clock restarts with the new entity or is carried forward via a succession clause. SEBI has not published a succession circular yet; be conservative.
